title: Apple Spends Billions to Buy News Rights: Introducing Real-Time News for AI Version of Siri, Pay-Per-Use Becomes a New Trend
excerpt: According to informed sources, Apple is in talks with multiple publishers for new content partnerships, aiming to enhance the capabilities of its AI-powered Sir
content_html:
According to informed sources, Apple is in talks with multiple publishers for new content partnerships, aiming to enhance the capabilities of its AI-powered Siri by leveraging news and information. The updated version of Siri is expected to be released later this year. In recent months, Apple has approached several publishing institutions to sign multi-year agreements to obtain content licenses that will support Siri AI in providing the latest news and information.

Differing from the licensing approaches typically used by large AI companies, Apple's proposal may involve a flexible payment mechanism—only paying publishers when their content is actually used by Siri. Sources said Apple has discussed potential payment arrangements that could reach hundreds of millions of dollars. Traditionally, AI companies' licensing deals with news organizations often include guaranteed fees and cover broad content access. Apple's proposed usage-based payment model is quite unconventional, and Apple has not commented on it.

A Key Step in Siri's Reinvention: Addressing Weaknesses and Avoiding Risks

The current negotiations come as Apple accelerates its efforts to reinvent Siri. As the voice assistant covering the Apple ecosystem, Siri has long been criticized for its lack of practicality. Apple previously announced a major upgrade to it, integrating AI capabilities more deeply to make it more suitable for daily use scenarios. Introducing real-time news is clearly aimed at enabling Siri to compete with rival conversational AI in information query scenarios, addressing its "lack of real-time information" weakness.

Apple has had prior preparations. Since launching its paid subscription service Apple News+ in 2019, Apple has continuously collaborated with publishers and has already obtained content access rights, including AI training rights, through certain agreements. News Corp, the parent company of The Wall Street Journal, still provides news content for Apple services. However, Apple has also learned lessons in AI news features: the AI-generated news summaries launched at the end of 2024 sparked controversy due to incorrect headlines and were quickly discontinued. This time, obtaining content from publishers through a paid model is not only to provide real-time information for Siri's AI capabilities but also reflects Apple's dual considerations of reducing content accuracy and copyright risk while advancing AI news initiatives.

content_html_zh:
据知情人士透露，苹果正在与多家出版商就新内容合作进行谈判，旨在通过利用新闻和信息来增强其人工智能 Siri 的功能。 Siri 的更新版本预计将于今年晚些时候发布。 近几个月来，苹果已与多家出版机构接洽，签署多年协议，以获得内容许可，支持 Siri AI 提供最新新闻和信息。

与大型人工智能公司通常使用的许可方式不同，苹果的提议可能涉及灵活的支付机制——仅当 Siri 实际使用内容时才向出版商付费。 消息人士称，苹果公司已经讨论了可能达到数亿美元的潜在支付安排。 传统上，人工智能公司与新闻机构的许可协议通常包括有保证的费用并涵盖广泛的内容访问。 苹果提出的基于使用情况的支付模式相当非传统，苹果尚未对此发表评论。

Siri 重塑的关键一步：解决弱点并避免风险

目前的谈判正值苹果加快重塑 Siri 的步伐之际。 作为覆盖苹果生态的语音助手，Siri长期以来一直被诟病缺乏实用性。 苹果此前宣布对其进行重大升级，更深入地整合AI能力，使其更适合日常使用场景。 引入实时新闻显然是为了让Siri能够在信息查询场景上与竞争对手对话式AI竞争，解决其“缺乏实时信息”的弱点。

苹果公司早有准备。 自2019年推出付费订阅服务Apple News+以来，苹果不断与出版商合作，并已通过某些协议获得了包括AI培训权在内的内容访问权。 《华尔街日报》的母公司新闻集团仍然为苹果服务提供新闻内容。 不过，苹果在人工智能新闻功能方面也吸取了教训：2024年底推出的人工智能生成的新闻摘要因标题不正确而引发争议，并很快被终止。 此次通过付费模式向出版商获取内容，不仅是为了为 Siri 的 AI 能力提供实时信息，也体现了苹果在推进 AI 新闻举措的同时，降低内容准确性和版权风险的双重考虑。
